direction.name: The page is the object
direction.idea: Find the printed or physical artefact that already exists in the subject's world and build the page as that thing. A wedding site is the invitation card. A restaurant is its menu. A conference is the ticket; a record is its sleeve; a shop is the receipt or the swing tag; an archive is a stack of tabbed folders; a course is the syllabus sheet. The artefact supplies everything a template would otherwise invent: its proportions, its typographic manners, its way of grouping information. Visitors recognise the object instantly, which is why these pages feel specific.
direction.composition: The first screen shows the artefact as a single filled panel (paper colour on a contrasting ground) centred or offset, with believable proportions: a card at 5:7, a ticket at about 2.2:1 with a notch cut by `clip-path`, a menu as a tall sheet. All primary content lives on it, set the way that object is set: centred and symmetrical for an invitation, in tidy aligned columns for a menu or ticket. The ground behind is a flat colour or one full-bleed photograph. As the page continues, each section is another piece of the same stationery: a second card, a tear-off stub, a folded panel, always filled shapes with real edges (straight, notched, scalloped, perforated by a dotted `border` of round dots at 4px or more), never outlined boxes. The footer is the back of the object.
direction.typography: Take the manners of the artefact: a bookish serif with small caps avoided, or a blunt condensed face for tickets and posters. Sizes stay within what print would use relative to the panel; the name is large on the panel, details are small and exact.
direction.colour: Paper and ink plus the ground the paper sits on. Two or three flat colours in total, like a two-colour print job.
direction.imagery: Optional. One photograph behind the object, or small photographs placed on it like tipped-in plates. The object itself is the image.
direction.richness: Recognition. The shaped edges, the print-like alignment and the limited inks make a familiar object out of plain HTML.
direction.pitfalls: Choose an artefact that truly belongs to the subject, or it becomes costume. Shape the edges with fills and `clip-path`; an outlined rectangle with a thin border is not an object. Keep text sizes readable on a phone, where the object becomes full width with its shaped edge kept at top and bottom.

hero.name: Card over a dim room
hero.blueprint: A full-bleed, low-key photograph of the room fills the viewport, darkened with `filter: brightness(0.7)` so it reads as atmosphere. Centred over it is one square-cornered panel in a flat warm tone taken from the photograph: columns 4–10, about 55% of the width and 62% of the height, a filled programme card with 32px padding. Along its top edge the three words of the title are spread to the left, centre and right in bold condensed capitals at clamp(28px, 2.5vw, 38px); that line is the headline. Under it sit two left-aligned blocks in the same face and size, line-height 1.0: the facts (date, time, place) as three short lines, then one supporting sentence held to 30ch. Along the card's bottom edge: a credit at left in 14px, the single action as a solid rectangular button in the centre, one text link at right. There is no navigation outside the card. The card is `position: sticky`: as the page scrolls it shrinks with `transform: scale` toward the bottom-left corner and stays there as a ticket-sized stub while photographs of differing sizes pass on a flat ground.
hero.mobile: The photograph fills 100svh and the card sits centred at full width minus 16px margins, 70svh tall. The title words stack as a two-line heading at 9vw at the card's top-left. The facts and the supporting sentence follow at 5.2vw in the condensed face. The action button spans the card's bottom edge. On scroll the card shrinks to a 120px stub pinned bottom-left.
hero.headline: The event or venue name, three words at most and up to about 8 characters each, spread across the card's top edge; two lines on a phone.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Hold it for about one screen per step and three screens at most, two held stages per page at most, with a line of text on every held screen. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Total and its receipt
sections.blueprint: A total at giant size, and beside it the slip that adds up to it. Left, columns 1–6: at the top the heading, two to five words at 40–44px, with a two-line note at 16px; at the bottom-left, anchored to the section's lower edge, the total at clamp(160px, 18vw, 300px) with leading 0.8, and one caption line at 17px under it. The space between heading and total is left empty. Right, columns 8–11: a paper-coloured slip 380–440px wide on the section's contrasting ground, top-aligned with the heading, its bottom edge a zigzag made with clip-path. The slip lists eight to fourteen rows in the text face at 15–16px with tabular numerals, grouped under bold group names; each row has a description on the left, a right-aligned value, and a leader of round 4px dots between. The last row is inverted on a solid ink bar and repeats the total. The slip's values must truly sum to the figure.
sections.mobile: Heading and note come first. The total follows at 40vw, flush left, with its caption. The slip comes last at full width minus 16px margins with its zigzag edge, rows at 15px, and the inverted total row closing it.

sections.name: Capabilities as a menu
sections.blueprint: The capabilities are set as a printed menu or price list. One paper-coloured sheet, 520–600px wide and taller than it is wide, sits on a contrasting flat ground, centred or starting at column 2; its top and bottom edges are cut into shallow scallops or a zigzag with clip-path, its sides straight. On it, centred at the top, the heading: two or three words at 44–56px, then 40px of space. Below, items in two or three groups; each group opens with its name at 20px bold. Each item is a row: the name at 19px on the left, a short value on the right (a price, a time, a quantity, 'included'), and between them a leader of round 4px dots (border-bottom: 4px dotted, sitting on the baseline). A description at 15px in the soft ink sits under the name, at most 34ch. 18px between items, 44px between groups.
sections.mobile: The sheet fills the width minus 12px margins and keeps its cut top and bottom edges. Names stay left and values right on one line with the dot leader between; descriptions wrap beneath at 15px. Group names drop to 18px. Padding inside the sheet is 20px.

sections.name: Output slips along the edge
sections.blueprint: For subjects whose result is a piece of text or paper: a receipt, a note, a ticket, a written line. A full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 96svh, sets the scene. In the upper centre, left-aligned in a column starting at 18% of the width, two short paragraphs in paper colour at 28–32px, the first opening with the heading's two to four words; a neutral scrim sits behind that column only. Along the bottom, six paper-coloured slips stand side by side across the full width with 12px gaps, each a filled rectangle of a different height (between 26 and 44svh), their lower ends cut off by the section's bottom edge. Two or three of the slips, not all, are tilted by 1–2 degrees. Each slip carries a sample of real output in the text face at 15px: a bold first line, a divider made of typed characters, then four to eight lines.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 100svh. The paragraphs sit in the top third at 22px. Only three slips show, each 30vw wide, standing along the bottom at different heights, and the row scrolls sideways to reveal the rest. Slip text stays at 14px; do not scale it down.

sections.name: Stacked folders with tabs
sections.blueprint: Projects are filed as folders: four to six full-width flat colour bands stacked so that each shows a 64px strip above the next, built with `position: sticky` and increasing `top` offsets (0, 64, 128px) so the bands pile up as the page scrolls. From the top-left edge of each band one or two tabs rise: filled shapes 44px tall and 200–320px wide with shouldered corners cut by `clip-path: polygon()` or an inline SVG path, side by side with 6px gaps, each in a flat colour that contrasts with its band. The project name sits inside the tab at 26–28px; the category sits right-aligned in the band's visible strip at 15px. An open band is 80svh: a 16:10 photograph in columns 1–7 and, top-aligned in columns 9–12, a 60-word description with a link. A two-word heading at 32px precedes the stack.
sections.mobile: Bands do not stick; they stack in normal flow, each led by one tab 40px tall with the name at 20px and the category beside it. Inside a band the photograph is full width at 4:3 with the description beneath at 16px and 20px padding.

sections.name: Founder's letter
sections.blueprint: A letter in a centred column 520px wide with at least 160px of empty ground above and below. At the column's top-left, a round portrait 44px across. 28px below it, four or five short paragraphs at 16–17px with leading 1.55, each two to four lines and separated by one blank line, written in the first person. No heading. The sign-off is the writer's name at 22px in the text face's italic, with the role at 14px in the soft ink beneath it. One phrase in the letter may carry a flat marker-colour background. Variant for a page built as an object: the letter sits on a filled paper-colour sheet 640px wide with 60px padding on a contrasting ground, square corners, its bottom edge cut into small scallops with `clip-path`, and below a row of 5px round dots a tear-off strip 72px tall that carries the email address.
sections.mobile: The column takes the full width with 24px margins; text at 16px, portrait 40px. In the sheet variant the sheet spans edge to edge with 24px padding and keeps its shaped bottom edge; the tear-off strip stacks the email above a full-width button.

sections.name: Clip-out coupon form
sections.blueprint: The form is a coupon to cut out. One filled card in a strong flat colour, about 2.2:1, spans columns 2–11 with a 14px radius, with 120px of ground above and below. Semicircular notches 28px across are cut into its top and bottom edges at the 46% mark with `clip-path` or an SVG `mask`, and a vertical row of round dots (a dotted `border-left` 5px thick in the ground colour) joins the two notches as the perforation. Left of the perforation, with 48px padding: a two-line heading of three to five words at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px) in heavy capitals at the top, and one sentence at 16px at the bottom. Right of it: four inputs stacked with 10px gaps, each a filled block 52px tall in a lighter tone of the card with its placeholder at 16px, then a full-width solid submit bar 56px tall in the darkest ink. Inputs keep visually hidden `label` elements.
sections.mobile: The card turns upright and spans the width with 12px margins. The perforation becomes horizontal: notches on the left and right edges, dots across. Heading and sentence sit above it; the four inputs and the submit bar sit below, each 54px tall.

sections.name: The reply card
sections.blueprint: The invitation to act is a printed card lying on the page. On a dark or strongly coloured flat field about 80svh tall, a paper-coloured panel 44vw wide with 7:5 proportions sits in columns 6–12, rotated two degrees, with its lower edge hanging 60px past the section's bottom so the section crops it. On the card, with 48px padding, everything is centred the way stationery is: a heading of two to four words at 32px, one or two lines at 17px, then the action as a solid bar across the card's full inner width, 56px tall, in the ink colour with paper-coloured text. Columns 1–4 hold only a short paragraph at 20–24px in the field's light ink, bottom-aligned 64px above the edge. The card is a plain filled rectangle with square corners and no outline; its rotation and crop make it an object.
sections.mobile: The paragraph comes first at 20px. The card follows at 90% width, tilted one degree, centred, its bottom edge still cropped by the section. Heading at 24px, lines at 16px, and the action bar 52px tall across the full inner width of the card.

sections.name: The back of the card
sections.blueprint: The footer is the reverse side of the page's artefact, laid out as the back of a postcard. A paper-coloured panel spans columns 2–11 on the contrasting ground, about 420px tall, its top edge cut into a row of twelve semicircular scallops (an inline SVG path or `clip-path`, each scallop about 100px wide). The panel is divided by space into two halves. Left half: a short sign-off of two to four words at 32px, then two or three lines at 16px, written like a message. Right half: the address block, four left-aligned lines at 18px with 12px between them, each line a link (email, telephone, street, social); above it in the top-right corner, a stamp: one small photograph, 3:4 and 88px wide, with a 6px paper-coloured margin. Along the panel's bottom edge, a single centred line at 12px gives the copyright like a printer's imprint.
sections.mobile: The panel runs full width with six scallops across its top edge. The stamp sits top-right at 64px wide; the sign-off and message come first, then the address lines at 17px beneath them, then the imprint line centred at 12px.

references.name: The Deep End
references.idea: The whole site is one invitation card floating over ambient footage, which shrinks into a pinned corner ticket as scattered stills scroll past.
references.hero: Full-bleed, dim, amber-toned video of a listening room: a modular synth and speaker at top, a person lying on a silk cushion in soft focus. Centred over it is a square-cornered panel about 55% of the viewport wide and 62% tall, a blurred brown-to-taupe wash. Inside, the three words of the title are spread along the top edge at left, centre and right in bold condensed caps. A small line-diagram logo sits below. Two left-aligned text blocks at 2.5vw in the same heavy condensed face, tightly leaded: five lines of event details, four of description. Bottom edge: credits left, an RSVP box centre, a small link right. No navigation.
references.type: PP Neue York extra-bold condensed is the only face, used at essentially one size, 36px, in white with very tight leading; credits drop to about 12px. Mixed case with occasional all-caps lines and a raised underlined ordinal. Hierarchy comes from spacing and position alone.
references.colour: #2b2216 #bda38b #c8874a #f1f1e9 #181818 — Warm browns and ambers lifted straight from the footage: dark walnut video, a taupe translucent card, then a flat tan page with honey-lit photos. White type only; no accent colour.
references.imagery: Low-light cinematic video and stills of people lying with eyes closed, shallow focus, amber backlight, wood panelling. Square-cornered and at very different sizes, from small thumbnails to near full-height frames, placed off-grid on flat tan.
references.layout: After the full-bleed opener the page becomes a flat tan field where photos are placed irregularly, one small at left, one mid-size near centre, one tall at right, with wide gaps. The invitation card stays pinned top-left. About four screens, no headings or sections.

sections.description: Flat tan background. Images sit at irregular positions and scales with no shared grid: a small landscape still about 14% wide near the left edge, a mid-sized one about 16% wide lower and nearer the centre, then a large portrait frame about 26% wide and a full viewport tall near the right. One video frame returns nearly full-bleed between them. No captions; all text lives in the pinned card, which partly overlaps the images.

On scroll the invitation panel collapses to a card pinned in the top-left corner, about half the viewport wide and 22% tall, flush with the edges. It keeps the three-word title spread along its top, the logo, five lines of date and address, and the RSVP box centred on its bottom edge. Its fill is semi-transparent taupe with a blurred dark vignette, so photos passing beneath tint it.

steal: Spread the words of a short title to the left, centre and right of a card's top edge so the name becomes its frame.
Set every line of an invitation in one heavy condensed face at one size and let line breaks and gaps create the hierarchy.
Shrink the hero card into a pinned corner ticket that keeps date, place and the RSVP button visible for the whole scroll.

references.name: Le Petit Bleu
references.idea: The cafe's teal-and-white stripes become the whole system: one teal ink on cream, everything boxed in thin double outlines like printed menu cards, beside a permanently visible photo of the room.
references.hero: Viewport split 50/50 with 12px gaps. Left: a cream panel with a thin pale-teal outline and rounded corners. Inside, a second outlined box is the nav bar: two-line hamburger left, teal brush-script logo about 300px wide centred, a caps order link right. Below, a two-line light serif headline at about 3.5vw, centred, in teal, then two centred stacks, each a bold caps label, a serif line and a solid teal button wrapped in a second thin outline. Right: a full-height rounded photo of a striped booth, with an outlined hours bar across its top, three slide dots bottom-left and a white address card bottom-right.
references.type: Self Modern, a light bookish serif, for headline and 15px body; Matter SQ bold caps for labels and buttons; Archive Mono Pro typewriter caps for menu rows; a brush-script logo. Section titles are tall condensed serif caps sized so four to seven letters fill the column.
references.colour: #fcfbf7 #13a7b2 #058599 #cfe5e7 #e9b81f — Cream paper and a single teal used for every word, rule, outline and button; no black anywhere. Yellow, floral reds and marble enter only through the interior photographs.
references.imagery: Bright, saturated interior and food photographs; the right-hand panel is a full-height slideshow with rounded corners. Small food shots sit in a horizontal strip, and a fine line drawing of the shopfront with one teal awning fills a card.
references.layout: The left half scrolls as a stack of outlined cream cards (full-width or two-up) with 12px gaps while the right half stays fixed. Card contents are centred. A sticky nav card rides over the stack. On mobile the photo becomes the hero card's background.

sections.description: A card containing only the section word in tall condensed serif caps, teal, sized so its four letters fill the column edge to edge. Below it, a stack of full-width outlined rows about 36px high, each with a category name in typewriter mono caps at left and a thin plus sign at right, separated by 6px gaps. Above the title: a ticker row of tiny caps and a strip of four small food photos with rounded corners.

The same giant condensed title treatment, then centred serif paragraphs in teal with underlined links in a narrow measure of about 280px. Further down, a landscape photo of the two proprietors with a centred two-line caption in tiny sans, followed by more centred paragraphs. All of it lives in the left half while the right photo panel has advanced to a shelf-wall image.

A header row with a tiny bold caps label at left and a script follow-us link with arrow at right, then three portrait images (about 3:5) with 12px rounded corners in a row, the third cropped by the column edge to imply a carousel. Directly below, the next giant section title begins and is cropped by the viewport.

steal: Print everything in one brand ink on cream, including body text, rules and buttons, and let photographs supply the other colours.
Wrap buttons and panels in a second thin outline offset by a few pixels to get a printed-ticket feel.
Keep a tall photo panel fixed on one half and scroll a stack of cards on the other, swapping the photo as sections change.

references.name: The state of the gallery
references.idea: A year-in-review told as a flight over a glowing particle landscape, where each statistic or pick is a single word floating in 3D space.
references.hero: The desktop capture caught the loader: a blue-black screen with a faint dot grid, a 4px acid-yellow progress bar across the top edge, the small logo centred at the top, and a percentage counter at 13.9vw (200px) in thin pale blue-grey grotesk anchored bottom-left. The loaded hero, seen on mobile, splits the title in two: the first two words top-left and the last three bottom-right at the same giant size, with a centred uppercase paragraph between them, all over a full-bleed terrain of olive-green haze and yellow particles. Tiny capital labels occupy all four corners.
references.type: Overused Grotesk only, regular weight: display words at 5 to 14vw in pale blue-grey with a faint lilac sheen, small parenthesised counts set as superscripts beside them, and 10px uppercase captions and corner labels. Two sizes and no bold.
references.colour: #08090d #515721 #b9c6cd #e6f21a #c8b9ee — Blue-black ground; the olive-to-acid-yellow glow of the particle field is the single colour. Type is cool pale grey with a lilac tint, and the yellow loader bar is the brightest element.
references.imagery: A procedural landscape of soft olive fog ridges with thousands of yellow-white points streaming toward the horizon in perspective; later, a curved floor of small tilted white tiles standing for catalogued sites. No photographs.
references.layout: One pinned canvas with a text overlay. Four corner labels stay fixed; each scroll step puts a single word or name at the centre with a one-line caption beneath it in the lower third. Nothing else appears on screen.

sections.description: Full-bleed particle terrain. One category word is centred at about 5vw in pale iridescent grotesk, with its count in parentheses set small and raised at the word's top-right like a superscript. A single-line uppercase caption at 10px sits centred roughly 20% below. Behind the word the particles briefly cluster into the shape of a large numeral. Corner labels are unchanged.

A top-pick slide: a tiny uppercase label above, then the pick's name centred at about 5vw and partly occluded by the scene. Below it dozens of small white rectangular tiles lie on a curved, receding floor grid, some flat and some tilting up toward the camera, growing larger toward the bottom edge of the viewport. A one-line caption sits under the name.

steal: Split a title in two and pin the halves to opposite corners, top-left and bottom-right, at the same giant size with the supporting paragraph centred between them.
Attach a count to a big word as a small parenthesised superscript at its top-right instead of building a stat card.
Make the loading percentage the first giant typographic element, anchored bottom-left under a full-width accent progress bar.
references.media: One fixed WebGL canvas is the only surface: a particle landscape covers 99% of the first screen with the title straight on it, and as you travel the particles leave the ground to form numerals, a figure, floating screenshot cards and a tile-grid panel, while streams of thumbnail tiles fly low between beats. No img or video elements.
references.motion: A percentage preloader is still at 89% at 4.5s, though the load event fired at 2.1s; after it the wheel is captured, each step easing the camera forward to the next beat, with text-free fly-through steps between them (5 of 13 screens show only terrain). Characters rise with a stagger, transform and opacity over 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) on 704 spans, 0.42s for secondary lines, and counts pop in with an overshoot from 0.6 to 1.08 to 1.
